items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: I met Barney Kessel up there when he came to town.

ctx.x: Yeah, once in a while he makes a record or something, and he still sings...

Yeah. I made a record with him where he played alto and flute, with Barney Kessel. Not too long ago, a couple of years ago... More than that. Five or six or seven years ago. He sounds beautiful. But he's around Frisco, and he's still playing very, very pretty. In fact, of all the solos on Four Brothers, I'll take his. It's the prettiest.

And so, I turned that job down. I'm stayin' in L.A. I'm not going anywhere. And I was existing, and I was happy; you know, I'd play with these different bands and stuff, you know. So all of a sudden, I get the call from Jerry Gray to play the Bob Crosby Radio Show, and that lasted for four years. And that's when I started recording, with the Modernaires, during the late Forties, about '47 or something like that. Then I started making recordings, and people started hiring me for recordings.
